articles.title: 3,000 Exploding Stars Just Gave Us a Big Clue About Dark Energy
articles.summary: Scientists studied almost 3,000 exploding stars called supernovas. Their results hint that dark energy — a mysterious force that pushes the universe apart — might be changing over time, not staying the same.

articles.title: Ancient Builders Dragged 55,000-Pound Stones 11 Miles — And We Finally Know Where From
articles.summary: New research shows ancient builders hauled 25-tonne stones at least 11 miles to build Britain's tallest stone row, the Devil's Arrows. Scientists traced the stones to a site called Brimham Rocks.

articles.title: Scientists Spy on Boobies with Tiny Backpack Cameras
articles.summary: Scientists traveled to a remote island to study red-footed boobies. They attached tiny cameras and trackers to the birds to learn where they fly and how they catch fish.
